findings.reason: without the edge the queue releases §7 first, spending about 13 hours of local-lane work to reproduce the defect the plan has just decided to fix first.
findings.text: the declaration table gives s7 `depends-on` only `iter-signal-context-and-enrichment#s6`, yet the lead's recorded decision `field-code-meanings-next` (plan.html:149) answers "built before the full-catalogue enrichment and the sibling-signal relations", and §7's descriptions consume the quantity/unit/role values §12 decides plant-wide; §7 is therefore releasable now that §6 is `done`, and its run (31,245 groups and 62,490 calls per the §6 landing record) would write the whole catalogue's descriptions from the same role scarcity §12 exists to repair, reproducing at scale the sibling-identical descriptions §12 cites at plan.html:98

findings.reason: the node can land complete with the motivating condition unchanged, leaving the sibling-relation work that follows still blocked on roles and the section's stated purpose unserved.
findings.text: the setpoint measure is two clauses that together cannot fail on the point §12 was created for: "a query for the setpoint role ... returns only signals carrying it" holds vacuously on an empty result, and the positive half is "at least one signal across the facility is decided as a setpoint or the record says plainly that none is and why", so a landing with zero setpoints decided anywhere satisfies the done-when while §12's own rationale (plan.html:98) names "no setpoint is decided anywhere, so no signal can be related to the one it is measured against" as the defect

findings.reason: the only guard against §12 regressing values §11 already decided has no failing condition, so a plant-wide table that contradicts the pilot's own metadata lands as a pass.
findings.text: for the pilot system the comparison is "the number unchanged, newly decided, and changed, with every changed value listed privately and read by hand", and unlike §12's other readings (at most one wrong in thirty entries, at most two wrong in thirty signals) this one states no tolerance, so a role or quantity correctly decided under §11 and changed wrongly by the field-code table is recorded but cannot fail the node

findings.reason: the status change rests on a record that does not carry two of the measures that close the section, so the plan asserts a completion its own record cannot show.
findings.text: the new landing record that carries §6 to `done` (plan.html:20 declares `s6: done`) omits two items its own done-when requires: "a search recorded in the landing record" that finds one path by which a group description reaches its members, and the requirement that no member description state a value the vocabulary does not hold for that signal (the record reports 180 signal-quantity / 188 unit / 16 role but not that none is unsupported)

findings.reason: the worker that finds this gate heavy has no partition named in the section and must choose one itself, which the plan's other heavy sections never leave open.
findings.text: §12 runs the §11 vocabulary assignment "over every catalogued signal of the facility", which §5 counted at 995,006 variables, and names no compute partition, while §3, §7 and §10 each state where their heavy run executes (`rigel`, `rigel`, `all_debug`); a plant-wide graph pass is a heavy job under the project's own compute rule
